utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The four documents of the Serbian ministry and foreign affairs I think need an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 792. I think Judge Kwon already mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And the clips of extracts from The Fall of Milosevic film.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Your Honours, I understand that, as to next week, the witness listed for Tuesday is only available on Tuesday. I've explained to Ms. Anoya that, as I see it, he is undoubtedly a witness who will last more than one day and we're having a number of these witnesses at the beginning of the Defence case. This is Mr. Primakov, and if his evidence is going to cover broadly similar types of topics as that which were covered in this witness's testimony, it's highly unlikely that it will be concluded in one day. Indeed, we'd always forecast him as a more substantial witness than this one. I don't know if there's any possibility of his being extended from the Tuesday to the Wednesday. Obviously we will take whatever is available, but we would be assisted by knowing what the plans are. And if not, who comes on the Wednesday?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you have given an estimate here of 2.5 hours for Mr. Primakov's -- who are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It's Mr. Primakov on the 30th, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. 2.5 hours. Isn't that an underestimate?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I abide by what I said. We had an agreement that he would take up only one day, and I will take up only as much time as I can, leaving Mr. Nice enough time for his cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is the situation that there is some very pressing business that would require him to return on Tuesday? I am thinking of the possibility that he may run over to the next day.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is not possible to extend his stay. And my examination-in-chief will not go beyond the time limit that leaves Mr. Nice adequate time for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the accused seems to have missed the point, I think. It is not for him to identify the amount of time I will require for cross-examination. These are obviously potentially very interesting witnesses and, depending on whether their evidence is relevant, the Chamber may be assisted by more rather than less questions. There may be time for adjusting downwards the amount of time I take of later witnesses. It simply isn't open to the accused -- he doesn't run the timetabling of the Court, and contingency plans ought to be made. Mr. Primakov, I think, I'll just check, I think he now holds the office of Chamber of Commerce, is it, or have I got it wrong? He was a Prime Minister, but he's now something rather different. And before the witness turns up to say in strict terms that he's only available for one day and no more has to be a pretty good reason for it. It's for the Chamber to decide --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I quite agree. Mr. Milosevic, I'm going to suggest your approach to this is a little too mechanical. We have to see what kind of evidence he's going to give, the kind of cross-examination that will be required. There's a qualitative element that you can't entirely predict, and I'd like you to have in mind that this witness may run over to the following day. That will be --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What Mr. Nice said is quite true. Evgeni Primakov was Prime Minister. Before that he was foreign minister. I'll not enumerate all his offices. It's not true that he works in the ministry of commerce now. He is president of Russia's Chamber of Commerce at this moment, the Chamber of Commerce of the Russian Federation. But bearing in mind the time that I need, I didn't have a long examination in mind, I thought I could manage within the time that I planned, and I thought that leaves Mr. Nice enough time. I don't think it was my duty to ask the witness to be able to stay for two days. I need only half of one day, and that's why he was planned for only one day, the day when he was scheduled. And I will try to use even less time than I originally planned, to leave Mr. Nice even more than 60 per cent of my time, but I don't think he's entitled to ask for more than 60 per cent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, as I said, we can't approach it in such a mechanical manner. What I say to you is that we'll hear Mr. Primakov on Tuesday, and you should be alert to the possibility, and he should be alert to the possibility that his evidence may run over to the following day. We are adjourned until Tuesday at 9.00 a.m.
